Isodiv Explorer

How internally diverse is each language lineage, measured as amount of lexical change (no clock, no counting of languages), and how far apart are different lineages? Data: ASJP v21 40-item word lists.

Maximum diversity per lineage

Dot: D_max at the calibrated scale. Line: how far the score moves when 10 of the 40 concepts are left out (5–95% of 30 resamples), centred on the dot; it does not include the effect of which doculects were sampled. 1.0 means one lineage; lineages with 2 doculects are lower bounds.

Diversity across scales

D_max as the similarity scale k changes (Z = exp(−k·PMI-LDND)). Small k lumps everything into one lineage; large k counts every distinct variety. Pick lineages to compare.

Mean PMI-LDND, within and between lineages

Diagonal: within a lineage. Off-diagonal: between two lineages. Click a cell to compare.
PMI-LDND 0 (identical)1 (unrelated)

What is measured

  1. Distance, not time. PMI-LDND on ASJP 40-item lists: LDND (Wichmann et al. 2010) with word distances from alignments scored by learned sound correspondences (pointwise mutual information, after Jäger 2013, 2018) instead of a flat cost per changed segment, so regular correspondences such as Japonic h : p count as close. Divided by the same measure for different meanings to remove chance resemblance. About 0 for identical lists and about 1 for unrelated languages.
  2. Diversity that ignores duplicates. Z = exp(−k·PMI-LDND), then the Leinster–Meckes maximum diversity D_max(Z): the effective number of fully distinct lineages. Adding another doculect that is identical to one already present does not change it.
  3. Scale without a clock. k is calibrated so two doculects of the same language (same Glottocode) are 0.9 similar. Here k_cal = .

Reading it

  • The calibrated scale is coarse. Two unrelated lineages (PMI-LDND ≈ 1) are still about 0.7 similar at k_cal, so their combined D_max stays small. The Between lineages view therefore also reports a finer scale (k = 3), where distinct lineages should add up.
  • Same-language doculect pairs differ by PMI-LDND (10th / 50th / 90th percentile). Lineages in the lowest band cannot be ranked against each other.
  • D_max measures diversity, not relatedness. Purple rows are constructed sets, not families: random sets of lects from unrelated families, and proposed or rejected groupings such as Altaic. Unrelated lects are as diverse as it gets, so random sets score at or above the deepest real families. A low score for a proposed grouping says its members are similar, which shared descent and long contact both produce; it is not evidence for or against the grouping. scripts/adversarial.py.
  • D_max is stable against duplicates, not against sampling more distinct varieties. Lineages with few doculects are lower bounds.
  • Contact shortens distances. The 40-item list resists borrowing but is not immune.
  • Doculects listed in config/exclusions.tsv are left out of every number here, each with its reason. scripts/audit.py flags candidates (far from the rest of the lineage, fewer than 30 of 40 concepts, or removing it lowers D_max by 0.015 or more) but never excludes automatically. A deep branch such as Chuvash is flagged and kept; a list distorted by contact or a transcription problem is excluded.
  • Samples: up to 80 doculects per lineage for diversity and profiles, 40 for the concept resampling, 25 for between-lineage comparisons, chosen round-robin across genera and Glottocodes.

Wichmann, Holman, Bakker & Brown 2010, Physica A 389. Leinster & Meckes 2016, Entropy 18(3). ASJP Database v21, CC-BY-4.0.
